newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico stocks end at sixth record February close.
newsitem.headline: Mexico stocks end at sixth record February close.

text.p: Mexican stocks drifted up to their sixth record close in February, boosted by foreign buying and ahead of expected falls in primary interest rates, traders said on Monday.
"The market responded well, buying was solid and foreign capital inflow was what helped," said a floor trader.
Final closing figures showed the leading IPC share index was up 9.73 points, or 0.25 percent, at a record close of 3,889.77. Trading volume was moderate at 74.5 million shares.
Traders said that inflation figures for the first half of February had little effect on dealing as they were released shortly before the close.
"The inflation figures were good, but had little effect as they came just as the market was taking profits," a desk trader said.
Banco de Mexico announced in late trade that consumer prices increased by 0.89 percent for February 1-15, compared to 2.57 percent for January as a whole.
A Reuters survey of financial houses in Mexico City showed they had expected an average increase of 0.88 percent.
The IPC reached an intraday high of 3,908.48 points in mid-morning trade before profit-takers stepped in.
Traders said forecast falls in primary Cetes rates spurred early buying.
"The market sees another slight fall in rates and the stable peso keeps the market on an even keel," an equity analyst said.
Dealers said foreign buyers were partly encouraged by a recovery on Wall Street after a downturn last week.
The Dow Jones ended up 1.10 percent at 7,008.20 points.
The most heavily traded gainer was financial group Bancomer whose B shares ended up three centavos at 3.18 pesos on what traders said was a technical recovery following recent falls.
Retail stock Comerci topped the decliners .PL.MX and was also the most heavily traded stock of the day .AV.MX, unseating Telmex into an unaccustomed second place.
Comerci UBC share units fell 46 centavos to 6.54 pesos.
"Dealers did not much like their buy of Kmart de Mexico, they were not convinced," a dealer said.
On the broad market, of 118 stocks traded, 60 ended up while 31 were down.
